notes:
Summary: Large fintech payments processor exploring Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing chat + internal fraud reranking. Wants predictable throughput and tight p95 latency SLOs for transactional workflows. Key ask: sizing workshop that converts sampled traces into GPU reservation guidance and SLA language for 99.9% availability + latency guarantees.

Observed workload patterns (from sample traces):
- Primary traffic: chat-based customer support (multi-turn), average session length 6 turns, median prompt length ~120 tokens, median response length ~160 tokens.
- Secondary traffic: real-time reranking of transaction flags (~200 QPS steady state, spikes to 900 QPS during peak clearing windows).
- Embeddings pipeline: nightly batch embeddings for new documents (~15M tokens/day) not latency sensitive.

Workshop objectives (customer):
- Establish baseline QPS and tokens/sec for steady-state and 99th percentile peak windows
- Map latency SLO targets to GPU pool sizing (target p90 < 120ms for short chat turns, p95 < 250ms for longer completions)
- Produce reserved GPU recommendation (instance types, count, cold-cache/head-of-line sizing) and autoscale guardrails
- Define fallback policies (region fallback, cheaper model variants) and explain cost tradeoffs (quantized variants, batching thresholds)
- Draft SLA amendment bullets: throughput guarantees, scheduled maintenance windows, incident notification timelines, credits for missed SLOs

Customer constraints and preferences:
- Must run in VPC; customer-managed KMS required for keys
- Data residency: primary US with EU failover; retention controls for PCI-adjacent data
- Strong cost sensitivity for high-volume reranking; prefers mixed model routing (dedicated for chat, burst to hosted for low-priority reranks)
- Prefers NVidia A100 or equivalent; open to q4_8 quantized runtime if quality acceptable

Open items / AE notes:
- Need to convert trace analysis into clear tokens/sec baseline before workshop; SE to provide analysis template (Ravi).
- Legal requested example SLA language for throughput guarantees — draft provided in Drive, awaiting legal redline.
- Procurement timeline is the gating item; suggested milestone-based payment (pilot -> production) to accelerate approval.
- Customer asked: "If we see 3x spike for <10 minutes, what fallback will preserve user experience?" SE proposed region fallback + async rerank queue.

Attachments and artifacts:
- Sizing deck v1 (Drive link above)
